juan-carrillo.text: Voted Aye on SB 79 (Wiener), requiring cities to allow denser housing near transit stations; Assembly floor, 09/11/25, passed 43-19.
Voted Aye on AB 130, the 2025 housing bill streamlining housing approvals and extending Housing Accountability Act protections; Assembly floor, 06/30/25, passed 62-3.
Voted Aye on SB 98, requiring notification at schools and colleges about immigration enforcement; Assembly floor, 09/02/25, passed 59-10.
Voted Aye on SB 81 (health and care facilities: information sharing); Assembly floor, 09/02/25, passed 58-11.
Voted Aye on SB 627 (law enforcement: masks) and carried it on the Assembly floor; 09/09/25, passed 45-23.
Voted Aye on AB 1127 (firearms: converter pistols); Assembly floor concurrence, 09/13/25, passed 54-16.
Voted Aye on AB 1207, extending California's cap-and-trade market-based compliance mechanism; 09/13/25, passed 58-10.
Voted Aye on ACA 8 (congressional redistricting); Assembly floor, 08/21/25, passed 57-20.
Authored AB 2533 (2024, signed): bars local agencies from denying permits for older unpermitted ADUs over building-standard violations and prohibits impact fees except for health/safety needs.
Authored AB 98 (2024, signed): statewide warehouse design standards, truck routing plans and buffer distances from homes and schools, with 2-to-1 replacement of demolished housing.

source.title: AB 98 - Logistics use and truck routes

juan-carrillo.text: Authored AB 1808 (chaptered 09/29/26): cuts mitigation fees for homeowners removing Western Joshua trees, lets cities authorize removals, and exempts certain permits from CEQA until 2032.

source.title: AB 1808 - Western Joshua Tree Conservation Act

paul-andre-marsh.text: "Our law enforcement agencies need adequate funding to support their operations, including personnel, equipment, and training." Also supports evidence-based programs addressing root causes of crime.
"Parents have a strong say in their children's education, healthcare, and well-being, without bureaucratic interference."
Advocates clear government spending reports so taxpayers understand fund use, eliminating wasteful spending and holding agencies accountable for performance.
Says police "deserve our full support" and prioritizes "supporting our officers"; backs building trust between law enforcement and communities.

notes: Marsh: thin; only a BallotReady profile and IJ Action page found, no campaign site retrievable (search budget exhausted). Carrillo evidence is mostly floor votes and authored bills.
